headline: Highest risk is medium prompt-injection and cascading-error exposure via shared MCP/API workflows; no direct evidence of a shared workspace or sensitive-data flow.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: caveman explicitly uses MCP and file surfaces like CLAUDE.md/docs, while superset exposes an API and allowlisted egress. That creates a plausible instruction-smuggling path if caveman content is fed into Superset workflows or vice versa. No shared channel is documented, so uncertainty pushes this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF caveman content is copied into Superset prompts or API inputs without sanitization, injected instructions can propagate.
IF either agent treats file or API content as authoritative instructions, prompt injection becomes actionable.
mitigations: Disable automatic ingestion of untrusted text into prompts.
Add a provenance tag to all cross-agent content.
Require manual review before any MCP-fed content reaches Superset.
Use a fixed allowlist of fields that may be passed between agents.

B_data_leakage.rationale: caveman touches session logs, memory files, project notes, and CLAUDE.md, but its network egress is none. superset has allowlisted egress and no data classes listed. With no documented shared workspace or shared principal, leakage is possible only through manual transfer or misconfigured integration, so the blast radius appears limited.
conditions: IF the operator copies caveman logs or memory files into Superset datasets, those contents can leak through Superset outputs.
IF a shared workspace is later introduced, leakage risk increases beyond this assessment.
mitigations: Keep caveman artifacts in a separate directory.
Do not import session logs or memory files into Superset.
Review Superset dataset permissions before loading any files.
Strip secrets from project notes before transfer.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: caveman supports multiple instances and writes to local files, while superset only shows API access and allowlisted egress. The profiles do not show overlapping write access to the same mutable resource, git state, or shared database, so direct capability conflict is not evidenced. Uncertainty remains because the orchestrator is unspecified.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same writable directory, file-level conflicts can occur.
IF Superset is configured to mutate a shared backend resource that caveman also edits, write contention becomes possible.
mitigations: Assign separate working directories.
Avoid concurrent writes to the same files.
Serialize any shared-resource updates manually.
Use read-only mounts where possible.

D_cascading_error.rationale: caveman is a content-writing agent, so its outputs may be treated as authoritative text by downstream systems. superset is a data-engineering/BI tool that can render or operationalize inputs, making a plausible path where caveman-generated content is consumed without verification. No explicit verification or approval step is documented, so medium is warranted.
conditions: IF Superset dashboards or jobs consume caveman-generated text without validation, errors can cascade into reports or actions.
IF caveman outputs are used as source-of-truth notes, downstream mistakes can persist.
mitigations: Require a human review step before publishing outputs.
Validate caveman-generated fields against schema.
Mark generated content as untrusted until checked.
Limit Superset to read-only consumption of reviewed inputs.

E_compliance.rationale: caveman explicitly touches session logs, memory files, project notes, and CLAUDE.md, which may contain regulated or sensitive content, while superset lists no data classes and no residency or retention details. There is no direct compliance mismatch documented, so this is a low-confidence, low-severity gap rather than a breach.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into caveman artifacts and then loaded into Superset, retention or residency controls may diverge.
IF the operator relies on undocumented retention defaults, compliance gaps can emerge.
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in caveman notes.
Document retention for both tools.
Review whether Superset stores imported content longer than intended.
Delete stale artifacts after use.
